Notes, not wake-up calls
A quick story from an earlier life: for years at the bedside, education meant getting handed a huge binder and a highlighter at the worst possible hour. Learning does not have to feel like that.
AI can help you study between shifts, in small pieces, on your schedule. But the boundary matters, so it is stated plainly: AI is education support here. It is never medical advice, and this newsletter will never tell you what to do for a patient or for yourself medically.
What AI is good at is the boring half of learning: restating things, checking that your explanation is consistent, keeping your notes short and calm, and making five minutes count.
The five-minute note-sketch
Pick one small thing you learned this week - one workflow idea, one systems concept, one thing that made your shift smoother. Ask an assistant to restate it in three plain sentences.
Read those three sentences, fix the two that are wrong, and keep what is left. That is a note that sticks, built by you, in five minutes.
This is education support. It is study hygiene, not clinical judgment - and the judgment stays with the people whose job it is.
